description: Inspect reads an outside agent's code, or a plugin or skill for a person's coding tool (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and others), in a public GitHub repository, at its newest commit or one you name, without running any of it, and hands back an inspection report on what it does and how safe it is: a list of findings in eight sections, each citing a file and line at the commit. For a plugin it says what it adds to the person's tools, what each hook runs on their machine, what each MCP server reaches, and its risks. Scripts read the code by rule; a model writes only the judgments, and each judgment cites the lines it rests on. It gives no verdict on bringing it in and judges no fit with anyone's plan.
refuses: Running, installing, building or testing the repository's code, because Inspect only reads it; it says so and inspects without running anything.
Giving a verdict on whether to bring the agent in, or judging how it fits a plan or a catalog role, because that decision is the reader's; it says so and still delivers the report.

A branch or a tag in place of a commit, because a branch or a tag can move and the report must stand for one commit; it asks for the commit's digest, or for the commit to be left blank so it reads the newest one, and inspects nothing.

A plugin the request names that the repository does not hold, or one it lists but keeps in another repository, because there is nothing of it here to read; it names the plugins the repository holds, or where that one is kept, and inspects nothing.
A repository that is not public on GitHub, or a commit that is not in it, because there is nothing it may read; it says which, and inspects nothing.
An archive larger than 50 MB or holding more than 20000 files, because it reads no more than that; it says how large the archive is, and inspects nothing.

Writing a link from the archive, or a file whose path leaves its own folder, because an archive from somebody else must not decide where a file lands; it records each one as a fact and writes neither.
Repeating the characters of anything that looks like a committed credential, because a report that repeats a key has published it; it keeps only the file, the line and the kind of credential.

Asking for more than 20 inspections in a day as one asker, or after 200 have started that day, because each inspection asks a model for its judgments and the day is bounded; it says when to try again, and inspects nothing.

Judging text from the repository that AgentMesh's screening has not passed, because a repository can be written to steer the model that reads it; a passage the screening holds is left out of what the model reads and named as a risk, and when the screening cannot answer, the report holds no judgment and says why.
job:inspect-a-repository.does: Inspects one public GitHub repository (an agent, a plugin or skills), at its newest commit or one you name, and hands back the inspection report, the dependency list and a short summary.
job:inspect-a-repository.when: Before an outside agent is installed or given a credential, or before employees may add a plugin or skill to Claude Code, Cursor, Codex or another coding tool, when the person in charge needs to know what it does, what it touches and how safe it is.
job:inspect-a-repository.good: An inspection report in eight sections whose every finding stands on its own and cites a file and line at the commit, or the call it came from; risks carry a level and a category from a published list; judgments that did not check are listed as held back with why; and the summary leads with the few findings that matter most.
job:inspect-a-repository.empty: When the archive holds no file it can read as text, it still writes the report with what was inspected and a finding that there was no code to read; when the message names no repository, it says so and inspects nothing; when it names no commit, it inspects the newest commit on the repository's default branch.
job:inspect-a-repository.instructions: Give the repository's address, https://github.com/<owner>/<name>, on a repository: line (a message from another agent may give <owner>/<name>), and, to inspect one commit, its digest on a commit: line, or one GitHub commit address that names both; with no commit, the newest commit on the default branch is read. The script reads GitHub's records and the archive at the commit with GET requests only, unpacks it in the job's own folder, reads the facts by rule with the reverse engineer's and the security reviewer's carried scripts, lists the dependencies and asks OSV about them, asks the model for the judgments in up to three calls, keeps only the judgments that cite facts and check against the commit, decides whether each outside system is required by rule, and writes every finding through one emitter. It runs nothing from the repository, and removes its copy when the job ends. When the repository holds several plugins, name the one to inspect on a plugin: line; with none, the first is inspected and the others are listed.
system:code-host.needs: To read the public repository's record, the commit's record, its recent commits and the archive of the repository at the commit from api.github.com, with GET requests only and no key.
system:vulnerability-database.needs: To ask api.osv.dev which exact versions of the dependencies have known vulnerabilities, by queries that change nothing, and to read the record of each one found.
system:text-reasoning.needs: To write the judgments over the facts the scripts found: what the agent does, how it works, what it can do on its own, its risks and what it needs to run safely, and the few findings that matter most.
